title: Concrete’s enabling role in building a sustainable and resilient future
gist: Oxford Economics report for the GCCA forecasts global construction rising over 70% to $16.6T a year by 2050 under five megatrends; only the summary is available.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics forecasts global construction activity to rise by more than 70% to US$16.6 trillion annually by 2050.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: Long-run demand tailwind for cement, concrete and building materials.

insights.claim: Five megatrends drive the outlook: population growth and urbanisation, infrastructure and housing deficits, climate transition and resilience, geopolitical uncertainty, and digitalisation.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: Framework for thinking about construction demand drivers.

insights.claim: The report, commissioned by the Global Cement and Concrete Association, highlights the challenge of meeting rising infrastructure demand while reducing carbon emissions, improving productivity and managing costs, and stresses innovation, resilient supply chains and evidence-based planning.
insights.speaker: Oxford Economics
insights.so_what: Industry-sponsored view; decarbonisation is the key constraint for cement.
